meta.title: One Word, and the Bit That Says Alive
meta.subtitle: An entity handle is 64 bits with no pointer in it — and the version field is what turns a dangling reference into a null instead of a disaster

views.label: The handle is one word
views.note: Eight bytes, three packed fields, no address anywhere. Comparing two entities is a single sixty-four-bit compare.

views.label: Index picks, version proves
views.note: The index selects a slot. The version in that slot must equal the version in your hand or the lookup refuses.

views.label: Detectable, not catastrophic
views.note: The same comparison produces either a chunk plus a slot number, or nothing. There is no third outcome.

views.label: Why indices come back
views.note: Indices are scarce and get reused. The version is the generation counter that keeps the reuse honest.

cards.title: What the version buys you
items: Twenty-eight index bits is 268 million slots, and they are recycled aggressively
Without a generation counter, a reused index silently addresses somebody else's data
With one, the stale handle fails a comparison you were already paying for
The slot lookup returns a null chunk rather than an address · EntityComponentStoreEntities.cs:72

cards.title: The liveness bit
items: A slot whose version has its low bit clear holds no live entity · EntityComponentStoreEntities.cs:55
Version zero is the null sentinel, and zero is even, so the rule stays consistent
The lookup short-circuits on version zero before it even touches the table · line 69
This is the same trick as an even-odd sequence counter in lock-free code
